speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you have a complex medical history; to begin, are you currently experiencing any cognitive changes, confusion, or visual disturbances alongside your gait and limb ataxia?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain, MRI Cervical Spine.
REQUEST TEST: Vitamin B12, Copper, and Ceruloplasmin levels.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML. MRI Cervical Spine: Normal Readings. Vitamin B12, Copper, and Ceruloplasmin levels: Normal Readings.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a crucial clue; natalizumab carries a risk of Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), but your history of Crohn's disease also raises the possibility of B12 deficiency or neurosyphilis mimicking ataxia. Given the potential for PML, have you noticed any new focal neurological deficits like weakness, numbness, or speech changes in the past few weeks?

REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with FLAIR and DWI sequences.
REQUEST TEST: JC Virus antibody test in CSF.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Brain with FLAIR and DWI sequences: Findings consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement. JC Virus antibody test in CSF: Positive.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given the confirmed PML and your history of Crohn's, I recommend immediately discontinuing natalizumab and initiating high-dose corticosteroids if there is acute visual or cognitive decline, while monitoring for potential rechallenge risks once JC virus status and clinical recovery are evaluated.
